id: 第一章-人性篇-大石内藏助的一天-intro-p1

en: 第一章-人性篇-大石内藏助的一天-intro
Warm, gentle sunlight fell on the closed sliding screens, and the artfully scattered shadows of an old plum tree's branches were cast across a row of paper window panels,
u.src: 温暖和煦的阳光洒在关着的拉窗上，老梅树枝错落有致的影子映在一排窗纸上，

en: The windows stretched from right to left and were roughly two or three jo long.
u.src: 窗户由右到左延伸开来，约莫有两三丈长。

en: Oishi Kuranosuke Yoshio, a retainer of Asano Takumi-no-kami, was at that time being held under the supervision of the Hosokawa family.
u.src: 浅野内匠头的家臣大石内蔵助良雄原，那时候正交由细川家监管。

en: He sat leaning against the sliding screen, knees together and posture formal, and had been reading intently for some time.
u.src: 他靠拉窗而坐，双膝并拢，正襟危坐，从刚才开始就在认真的看书。

en: It was probably a book lent to him by one of the Hosokawa family's retainers, a volume of The Three Kingdoms.
u.src: 一本约莫是细川家某位家臣借给他的书——《三国志》中的一本。

en: There were nine people in the room altogether.
u.src: 房间里拢共有九个人。

en: Kataoka Goemon had just gone to the toilet.
u.src: 片冈五右卫刚才去上厕所了。

en: Hayami Tozaemon had gone to the lower room to find someone to talk to and was slow to return.
u.src: 早水藤左卫门去到下房找人说话，迟迟未归。

en: The remaining six were Yoshida Chuzaemon, Hara Soemon, Mase Kyudayu, Onodera Junai, Horibe Yahei, Hazama Kihei, and the others.
u.src: 余下六人分别是吉田忠左卫门、原总右卫门、间濑久太夫、小野寺十内、堀部弥兵卫、间喜兵卫等。

en: No one paid any attention to the sunlight falling on the sliding screens; some bent over their books and read intently, while others were wholly absorbed in writing letters.
u.src: 没人在意洒在拉窗的阳光，他们中有的埋头认真看书，有的在全心贯注的写信。

en: Perhaps because the six who remained were all old men in their sixties or seventies, the room, warm yet still chilly, was utterly silent.
u.src: 可能因为剩下的这六个人都是六七十岁的老人，乍暖还寒的房间里寂静无声。

en: Even when someone coughed from time to time, the sound was so slight that it could not stir the scent of ink drifting in the air.
u.src: 就算不时有人咳嗽，但那声音也轻得无法震动飘荡在空中的墨香。

en: Kuranosuke raised his head from The Romance of the Three Kingdoms and gazed deeply into the distance.
u.src: 内藏助抬起头来不再看《三国志》，深深凝望远方。

en: Without saying a word, he held his hands over the brazier to warm them.
u.src: 他一言不发的把手放到火盆上方取暖。

en: A wire mesh covered the top of the brazier, and beneath it the charcoal was glowing red,
u.src: 火盆上面罩着铁丝网，下面是烧的火红的木炭，

en: the fiery red coals lit up the ash of the burned-out charcoal.
u.src: 火红的炭火照亮了燃尽的炭灰。

en: Kuranosuke was enveloped in the warm heat, and in his heart he felt deeply content.
u.src: 内藏助被温暖的热气笼罩，内心非常愉快。

en: On the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month last year, they avenged their late lord, and when they withdrew to Quanbing Temple, he had chanted, How splendid to wash away our hatred, though this body may be cast aside; the moon over the dusty world is hidden by no cloud.
u.src: 去年腊月十五日他们故主报了仇，当时撤到泉兵寺的时候，他曾吟道：“快哉雪恨身可舍，尘世之月无云遮。”

en: Today he once again felt the serene pleasure he had known then.
u.src: 今天他再次体会到当时怡然的心情。

en: Nearly two years had already passed since he withdrew from Ako Castle,
u.src: 自退出赤穗城已经有近两年的时光了，

en: He had poured enormous effort into planning it and was deeply anxious.
u.src: 他花费了大量心血去策划，很是焦虑。

en: Even just holding back those impatient, impulsive companions, keeping them from acting rashly, and waiting quietly for the right moment,
u.src: 就光是拦着那些急于求成、性格冲动的同伴，防止他们草率动手，静候成熟时机，

en: his hardship was far beyond ordinary.
u.src: 他的辛苦就非比寻常。

en: Moreover, spies sent by his enemy were constantly watching his every move.
u.src: 此外，仇人派来的细作一直在偷窥他的一举一动。

en: Outwardly he acted as if he had given himself over to dissipation, trying to deceive those spies,
u.src: 他表面上放浪形骸，企图遮住这些细作的眼睛，

ja: わされぬようにせねばならなかった。
en: while at the same time he had to make sure his own comrades were not misled by the false appearance of his dissipation.
u.src: 与此同时又一定得让自己的伙伴不要被自放浪的假象蒙蔽。

en: He thought back on the plans he had once discussed at Yamashina and Maruyama,
u.src: 他回忆过去自己在山科和圆山的计议，

en: and the painful feelings he could not voice then rose again in his heart.
u.src: 那时候说不出口的苦衷又在心头浮现。

en: But now everything had been settled, and his purpose had already been achieved.
u.src: 不过，现如今一切都已尘埃落定，目的已经实现了。

en: If there was still anything left unfinished, it was the shogunate's judgment on their band of forty-seven men.
u.src: 假如说还有什么没办完的事的话，那就是幕府对他们一伙四十七个人的处分。

en: The carrying out of that judgment was clearly not a matter of the distant future either.
u.src: 那处分的执行显然也不是很远之后的事情。

en: Indeed, everything had already settled, and their purpose had already been achieved.
u.src: 的确啊，一切已经尘埃落定，目的已经实现了。

en: Moreover, they had not merely completed the act of revenge; they had carried it out according to their own moral code, and this was undoubtedly a great success.
u.src: 而且不仅仅完成报复的行动，而且是按照他们自己的道德准则进行的，这无疑是巨大的成功。

en: He felt not only the achievement of having completed his undertaking, but also the satisfaction of having fulfilled his sense of morality.
u.src: 他不光有完成事业的成就感，还有实现道德的满足感。

en: Furthermore, whether considered from the aim of the revenge or from the manner in which it was carried out, this satisfaction was something that could stand before his own conscience.
u.src: 此外，不管是从复仇的目的来说，还是从复仇的方式来说，这种满足都是对得起自己的良心的。

en: What could be more worthy of satisfaction than this...
u.src: 还有什么比这更值得满足的呢……

en: As he thought it over, Kuranosuke smoothed his brow and, across the brazier, said to Yoshida Chuzaemon, "It is warm today, isn't it?"
u.src: 内藏助一边思考一边舒展开了眉头，隔着火盆，他对吉田忠左卫门说：“今天很暖和啊。”

en: Yoshida Chuzaemon seemed to have grown tired of reading; he rested the book on his knees and practiced writing by tracing characters with his finger.
u.src: 吉田忠左卫门可能是看书看累了，他把书放在膝上，用手指比划着练字。
他回复说：“不错啊。

en: The weather is fine, so let us just idle away the time like this until we feel sleepy."
u.src: 天气很好，就这么闲着，一直到想睡觉为止。”
内藏助露出微笑。

en: He remembered New Year's Day that year, when Tomimori Sukeemon had become drunk after drinking only three cups of toso sake.
u.src: 他想起今年春节那天，富森助右卫门喝了三杯屠苏酒就醉了。

en: He recited, "Today I welcome spring once more; even if I sleep at leisure, my heart feels no shame, for a warrior's wish has already been fulfilled."
u.src: 他吟道：“今日又迎春，纵然闲睡心无愧，武士愿已偿。”

en: This haiku was deeply meaningful, and its implication perfectly matched Yoshio's present feeling of proud satisfaction.
u.src: 这首俳意味深远，它的寓意与良雄现在志得意满的心情完美契合。

en: After all, the good work has been brought to a perfect close, so let us take a breath.
u.src: “毕竟是功德圆满了，歇口气吧。”

en: Yes, that must be the reason.
u.src: “不错，应该是这个缘故。”

en: Chuzaemon picked up the pipe at his side, filled it with tobacco, and quietly savored the fragrance of the smoke.
u.src: 忠左卫门拿起手边的烟袋，装上烟，文静地吟味着烟香。

en: The early spring afternoon was so bright and still; a wisp of bluish smoke he had breathed out rose softly and gradually vanished.
u.src: 早春的下午是那么明朗静寂，吐出来的一缕青烟袅袅上升，逐渐消失了。

en: None of us ever imagined we could still live such easy, contented days.
u.src: “咱们谁也没想过还能过上如此悠然自得的日子。”

ja: まったくそのとおりです
u.src: “的确啊。

en: I never even dreamed that I would live to see this spring.
u.src: 我做梦也没想到还能过上今年的春天。”

en: When you put it that way, we really have all been very lucky.
u.src: “这么说起来咱们还真都运气很好呢。”

en: The two looked at each other and smiled, both completely satisfied.
u.src: 两人对视微笑，都非常心满意足。

en: Just then, a figure appeared on the sliding door behind Yoshio,
u.src: ——此时，良雄背后的拉门上出现了一个人影，

en: One hand of the figure reached for the door pull; the shadow vanished, and the sturdy Hayamizu Tozaemon returned to the room.
u.src: 人影的一只手伸到门拉手上，影子便消失了，身材健壮的早水藤左卫门回到了房间。

en: If not for that, Yoshio would surely have gone on basking contentedly in the warm, gentle sunlight of early spring.
u.src: 如果不是如此，良雄一定还会心满意得的继续沉浸在早春温暖和煦的阳光里。

en: But when the ruddy-faced Tozaemon came smiling up to the two of them, he unceremoniously pulled them back into real life;
u.src: 然而当面色红润的藤左卫门面带笑容的地来到他俩面前，毫不客气的把他们拉回到现实生活里；

en: As for them, of course they had not noticed this.
u.src: 至于他们呢，自然没有察觉到这一点。

en: The servants' quarters seem quite lively.
u.src: “下房倒相当热闹呢。”

en: Chuzaemon said this while lighting a pipeful of tobacco.
u.src: 忠左卫门一边说着一边点燃了一袋烟。

en: Today happened to be Denemon's turn on duty, so the conversation was very pleasant.
u.src: “今天刚好是传右卫门官人值班，所以闲谈的甚是开心。

en: Kataoka and the others had also just come downstairs, and they sat there without leaving.
u.src: 片冈等人也是刚才到了下方，就坐在那不走了。”

en: No wonder he has not come back for so long.
u.src: “怪不得迟迟不归。”

en: Chuzaemon choked on the smoke and smiled in a hard-to-describe way.
u.src: 忠左卫门被烟呛了一下，难说的笑了笑。

en: Onodera Junai, writing furiously, seemed to be lost in thought,
u.src: 奋笔疾书的小野寺十内似乎若有所思，

en: He lifted his head slightly, but his gaze at once dropped back to the paper, and he went on writing earnestly.
u.src: 他抬了抬头，目光又马上落在纸上，继续认真写下去。

en: He was probably in the middle of writing a letter to his wife in Kyoto.
u.src: 他可能是正给在身在京都的妻子写信呢吧。

en: Kuranosuke narrowed his eyes and said with a smile, "Has there been any interesting news lately?"
u.src: 内藏助眯起眼睛笑着说：“最近有什么有意思的新闻吗？”

en: There was nothing at all; he was just talking nonsense as usual.
u.src: “什么都没有，就像往常一样瞎说呢。

en: However, when Chikamatsu had just told the story of Jinzaburo, Denemon and the others listened to the end with tears in their eyes.
u.src: 不过，方才近松讲起甚三郎的故事时，传右卫门官人等听完了，都眼含热泪。

en: Aside from that, though, now that you mention it, there really is something rather interesting.
u.src: 除了这事儿——的确，这么一说，还真有个有意思的事呢。

en: They say that ever since we killed Lord Kira, revenge has become the fashion inside Edo Castle.
u.src: 据说自从咱们杀了吉良官人之后，江户城内流行复仇啦。”
“哈哈，这倒真是意料之外呀。”

en: Chuzaemon glanced at Tozaemon in surprise.
u.src: 忠左卫门惊讶的看一眼藤左卫门。

en: For some reason, Tozaemon was extremely pleased whenever he told this story to others.
u.src: 不知道为什么，藤左卫门跟别人讲这个故事时，非常得意。

en: I have just heard two or three rather similar incidents,
u.src: “我刚才听说了差不多的两三件事，

en: and the funniest of them was the one that happened at noon in Minatocho, in Minami Hatchobori.
u.src: 其中最可笑的事是发生在南八丁堀的凑町中午的那件。
事情是这么发生的：

en: In a public bathhouse, the owner of a nearby rice shop got into an argument with a young man from the dye shop next door,
u.src: 在公共澡堂里，附近米店的老板跟隔壁染房的伙计吵了起来，

en: apparently over the trivial matter of bathwater from the dye shop worker splashing onto the rice shop owner.
u.src: 大概的缘故是染房伙计的洗澡水溅到了米店老板身上这种小事儿。

en: After that, the dye shop worker struck the rice shop owner with a water bucket and beat him up.
u.src: 后来，染房伙计用水桶砸了米店老板，把他揍了一顿。

en: Later, one of the rice shop's apprentices set out to avenge his master,
u.src: 后来米店的一个学徒为了给老板报仇，

en: At dusk, he ambushed the dye shop worker there and slashed into his shoulder with an iron hook.
u.src: 傍晚时分，他在那伏击了染房伙计，用铁钩砍进了染房伙计的肩膀。

en: It is said that even as he struck, he shouted, 'I am the strongest; I can avenge my master.'
u.src: 据说他在砍人的时候还一边喊着‘我才是最厉害的，能给我的主人报仇雪恨’。

en: As Tozaemon grew excited while talking, his gestures became somewhat animated.
u.src: 藤左卫门说到兴起有些手舞足蹈。
“真是无法无天啊。”

en: At first glance, it seems that the young fellow was seriously injured, but the neighbors around him actually sympathize more with the apprentice; it is really hard to understand.
u.src: “虽然看起来是那伙计受了重伤，但是周围邻居反而更同情那学徒，真是难以理解。

en: Besides that, there was one case in the third lane of Tongmachi, another in the second lane of Shinkyokumachi, and yet another somewhere else.
u.src: 此外，在通町三巷有一起，在新曲町二巷也有一起，还有什么地方也有一起。

en: In short, the same sort of thing is happening in many places.
u.src: 总而言之，很多地方都在发生类似的事情。

en: They say everyone is copying us. Isn't that strange?
u.src: 据说都是在学咱们呢，奇怪不奇怪？”

en: Tozaemon and Chuzaemon looked at each other and smiled.
u.src: 藤左卫门和忠左卫门互相对视而笑。

en: They must have been very pleased to learn that the revenge had affected the hearts of the people of Edo, however slight the change might have been.
u.src: 他们得知复仇的事情给江户人的内心产生的的影响，不管多么细微的变化，也一定是非常开心的。

en: Only Kuranosuke sat alone with one hand propping up his forehead, impatience on his face, saying nothing at all.
u.src: 只有内藏助一个人，他一手撑着额头，面露不耐，一声不吭。

en: He had been quite satisfied with himself, but Tozaemon's words cast an indescribable shadow over his heart.
u.src: 他原本对自己相当满意，藤左卫门的话，在他的心头投射出了不可言语的阴影。

en: Even so, he had no need to take responsibility for what he had done.
u.src: 虽然是这么回事，他没必要为自己做过的事负责任。

en: Even if revenge became fashionable in Edo Castle after they had carried it out, his conscience would still be clear.
u.src: 就算他们完成了复仇后，复仇在江户城内流行起来，他也对得起自己的良心。

en: Still, he felt that the passionate feeling which had filled his heart was cooling somewhat.
u.src: 虽然如此说，但他还是觉得自己心里原来漫漫的热烈情绪凉下去了几分。

en: Strictly speaking, at that moment he was merely surprised that his own group's revenge had produced such far-reaching effects in places he had never expected.
u.src: 认真说来，那时候他不过是对自己一伙人的复仇事件，竟然在想的没想过的地方产生了那么深远的影响，感到吃惊罢了。

en: Under ordinary circumstances, he would have laughed it off just as Tozaemon and Chuzaemon did.
u.src: 假如在平常，他会和藤左卫门和忠左卫门一样，笑笑算了。

en: Yet this fact still scattered a seed of displeasure into his self-satisfied heart.
u.src: 但是这个事实依然给他志得意满的心里洒下了不开心的种子。

en: That was probably because his satisfaction contained a certain amount of self-deception and, underneath, ran against the logic of the facts.
u.src: 这很可能是因为他的心满意足多少有点自说自话的成分，暗地里却与事实逻辑背道而驰吧。

en: Of course, at that time he had no thought of analyzing the matter logically.
u.src: 当然了，这个时候他没想过用逻辑来分析问题。

en: He merely felt a cold wind stirring in the depths of his triumph, and it gave him a kind of anguish that was hard to define.
u.src: 他不过是觉得志得意满的深处有股寒风冷气，这让他有种难以严明的苦恼。

en: But the other two did not notice that Kuranosuke was not laughing at these things.
u.src: 但是，其他两个人并没有注意到内藏助没有笑对这些事情。

en: Indeed, the honest and dutiful Tozaemon must have believed completely that Kuranosuke's interests were the same as his own.
u.src: 的确啊，老实本分的藤左卫门约莫百分百相信，内藏助和他本人的兴趣是相同的。

en: Otherwise, he certainly would not have gone downstairs himself and brought Horiuchi Denemon, the Hosokawa retainer on duty that day, into the room.
u.src: 要不然，他肯定不会自己去下方把细川家当天值班的家臣堀内传右卫门带到房间里来。

en: Still, he was an exceedingly earnest man,
u.src: 不过，他是个无比认真的人，

en: so he turned to Chuzaemon and said, "Call Master Denemon here,"
u.src: 他扭头对忠左卫门说，“把传右卫门官人叫来吧”，

en: then immediately slid open the partition and went happily and contentedly toward the lower room.
u.src: 就随即拉开隔扇，开心满足地走向下房。

en: Before long, still beaming broadly, he proudly came back into the room with the thoroughly plain and rustic Denemon.
u.src: 不多一会儿，他仍笑容满面，带着老师木讷朴的传右卫门得意地进屋了。

en: Oh my, you have gone to the trouble of coming in person; it is an honor to have you here.
u.src: “哎呀啊，竟劳您亲自前来，蓬荜生辉啊。”

en: As soon as Chuzaemon saw Denemon, he hurried to speak to him with a smile on Yoshio's behalf.
u.src: 忠左卫门一看见传右卫门，忙替良雄笑着跟他搭话。

en: Denemon was honest and dutiful by nature, and since Yoshio and the others had been placed under watch, they had already formed a bond like that of old friends.
u.src: 传右卫门为人老实、本分，良雄等人自从被监管以来，他们已经结成了老朋友一般的情谊。

ja: えたいのですが、やはり
en: I came in response to Brother Hayamizu's kind invitation. Although I did not want to disturb you, I have imposed on you after all.
u.src: “应早水兄盛情邀请而来，虽然不想打扰你们，但还是来叨扰了。”

en: After Den'emon sat down, he raised his thick eyebrows, the muscles in his dark cheeks twitching as if he were about to laugh, and quietly observed the people in the room.
u.src: 传右卫门坐下后，挑起着浓眉，黝黑的面颊上的肌肉抖动着要笑，私下观察屋里的人们。

en: Everyone returned the greeting in turn; whether they had been reading books or writing letters, they each exchanged courtesies with Den'emon, and Kuranosuke also spoke to him attentively.
u.src: 众人分分回敬，看书的也好，写信的也罢，都分别同传右卫门寒暄，内藏助也殷勤搭话。

en: Among them, the most comical was Horibe Yahei: he had set the unfinished Tale of the Taiheiki in front of him and was dozing with his glasses on,
u.src: 其中，颇为滑稽的是堀部弥兵卫，他把没看完的《太平记》放在面前，戴着眼镜打盹儿，

en: then at that moment he opened his eyes, hurriedly removed his glasses, and bowed his head with great respect.
u.src: 这个时候一睁开眼，慌忙摘下眼镜，恭恭敬敬地低头行礼。

en: At the sight, even Hazama Kihei laughed at the way Yahei seemed so overcome with admiration, then quickly turned his head toward the nearby folding screen and struggled to hold back his smile.
u.src: 看到这番场景，就连间喜兵卫也被他折服模样都笑了，连忙把头转向旁边的屏风，费力地绷住笑容。

en: Master Den'emon seems not to like old people, and he never comes here.
u.src: “传右卫门官人好像不喜欢老人，从来不来这里。”

en: Kuranosuke suddenly said something out of character, and his words came smoothly.
u.src: 内藏助突然反常发言，言语流利。

en: This was because, although he had been affected a little, his innermost heart was still filled with a triumphant sense of satisfaction.
u.src: 这是因为虽然受到了一点感染，但是他的内心深处还充斥着志得意满的情绪。

en: No, that is not the reason.
u.src: “不是的，不是因为这个原因。

en: But I was always detained by the people there, and time simply slipped away.
u.src: 但总是被那边的各位挽留，时间就那样过去了。”

en: I just heard that you were talking about something very interesting.
u.src: “我适才听说，你们在讲很有意思的事情呢。”

en: Chuzaemon also began to join the conversation.
u.src: 忠左卫门也开始搭话。

en: What I mean by “something interesting” is...
u.src: “有意思的事情——说的是……”

en: What I mean is that revenge has become fashionable everywhere in Edo.
u.src: “说的是江户到处都流行复仇了。”

en: Having said this, Tozaemon smiled as he looked at Den'emon, then glanced at Kuranosuke.
u.src: 藤左卫门说完，看着传右卫门微笑，又看了看内藏助。

en: Oh, so that is what you meant.
u.src: “哦，说的是那件事呀。

en: The human heart is truly very mysterious.
u.src: 人心真的是非常神奇的。

en: Seen this way, the common people are all moved by your loyalty and righteousness, and they want to learn from it too.
u.src: 这么看来，百姓们都被你们的忠义所感染，也都想学习呢。

en: It can have a great influence in changing the corrupt customs that run from the top down.
u.src: 在改变从上而下的堕落风俗，能够产生很大的影响呢。

en: Nowadays, only joruri and kabuki plays and the like, things we never really wanted to see, are popular, so this is a very good moment.
u.src: 现如今盛行的全是我们根本不想看的净瑠璃啦，歌舞伎剧什么的，因此是非常好的时机。”

en: From Kuranosuke's point of view, the conversation had begun to drift off course again,
u.src: 在内藏助来看来，谈话的走势又开始偏离轨道了，

en: So he deliberately made a few solemn-sounding humble remarks, hoping to use them to shift the subject deftly.
u.src: 因此他故意煞有其事的说了几句谦卑的话，想借此巧妙地转换话题。

ja: まことにありがとうございます。
en: Thank you very much for recognizing our loyalty.
u.src: “非常感谢您对我们忠义的认可。

en: But personally, my first feeling is shame.
u.src: 但是，我个人的想法是首先觉得羞耻。”

en: As he said this, he looked around at the people seated there.
u.src: 他说着，四下看了下在座的人们。

en: The reason is that although the Ako domain has many people, as you can see,
u.src: “这是因为，虽然赤穗藩的人口很多，但是正如你看见的那样，

en: those gathered here are mainly men of low rank.
u.src: 这里主要是身份卑下的人。

en: Of course, at first Okuno Shogen, the captain of the guard, took part in discussions of the plan,
u.src: 当然，一开始奥野将监警卫长参与了计划的磋商，

en: but he changed his mind midway and finally left the alliance, which is truly regrettable.
u.src: 但是他中途改变了注意，最后脱离了同盟，真是非常让人遗憾的。

en: Besides them, Shindo Genshiro, Kawamura Denbei, Koyama Gengozaemon, and others all held higher positions than Hara Soemon,
u.src: 除此以外，进藤源四郎、河村传兵卫、小山源五左卫门等人都比原总右卫门的地位高，

en: and Sasa Kozaemon and the others were also of higher rank than Yoshida Chuzaemon,
u.src: 佐佐小左卫门等人也比吉田忠左卫门的身份高，

ja: わりしてしまいました。
en: but when the moment came to launch the uprising, they all changed their minds.
u.src: 但是他们就要发动起义的时候，他们都变了心。

en: Moreover, among them were even relatives of mine.
u.src: 而且这里面还有我的亲属。

en: That is precisely why I feel such unbearable shame.
u.src: 正是因为如此，我才会感觉到无比羞耻。”

en: After Kuranosuke finished saying this, the mood in the room shifted from its earlier cheerfulness to a solemn atmosphere.
u.src: 内藏助说完这段话，屋里空气由先前的愉快转变成了严肃的气氛。

en: Seen from that point of view, he could be said to have changed the subject according to his own wishes.
u.src: 从这一点上来看，他可以说是按照自己的心思转换了话题。

ja: しませるものだったかどうかは、
en: But whether the conversation that followed would be pleasant for Kuranosuke is hard to say.
u.src: 但接下来人们的谈话能不能让内藏助感到愉快，就不好说了。

en: After hearing his lament, Hayami Tozaemon rubbed his fists together and said, "
u.src: 听完他的感慨，早水藤左卫门摩拳擦掌，说：“

en: They are all beasts with human faces and animal hearts.
u.src: 他们都是人面兽心的畜生。

en: They are utterly unworthy of being samurai."
u.src: 根本不配成为一个武士。”

en: Yes, people like Takada Gunbei are lower than beasts.
u.src: “是的，像高田群兵卫那种人，连畜生都不如呢。”

en: Chuzaemon raised his eyebrows slightly and looked toward Horibe Yahei, as if seeking his agreement.
u.src: 忠左卫门抬了抬眉毛看向堀部弥兵卫，好似要得到认同一样。

en: Naturally, the straightforward Yahei could not remain unmoved either:
u.src: 性情直率的弥兵卫当然也不会无动于衷：

en: On the very morning the uprising succeeded, we saw him,
u.src: “起义成功的当天早上，我们见过他，

en: I thought that even spitting in his face several times would not ease the hatred in my heart.
u.src: 我认为吐他几口吐沫都难消我心头之恨。

en: For he still had the shameless nerve to come before us,
u.src: 因着他还敢不知廉耻的来到我们跟前，

en: and say things like congratulations on the success of our uprising."
u.src: 恭喜我们起义成功什么的。”

en: “Takada is not exactly a good man either, but Koyamada Shozaemon and the others are all cut from the same cloth,” Mase Kyudayu muttered to himself.
u.src: “高田也不是什么好人，可是小山田庄左卫门等人也都是一丘之貉。”间濑久太夫喃喃自语。

en: In this way, Hara Soemon and Onodera Junai also began denouncing the traitors with shared indignation.
u.src: 就这样，原总右卫门和小野寺十内也同仇敌忾的骂起那些背叛者。

en: Even Hazama Kihei, who said nothing at all, kept nodding to show that he agreed with everyone, though he expressed nothing in words.
u.src: 就连一言不发的间喜兵卫，尽管没用语言表示什么，但也不停的点头以示对大家的赞同。

en: In any case, it is hard to imagine that such vile men could belong to the same domain as loyal retainers like you.
u.src: “无论如何，很难想象他们那些卑劣的人竟然和你们这些忠臣同处一藩。

en: Perhaps for that very reason, not only the samurai but even ordinary commoners despise those vile warriors who draw their stipends while doing nothing.
u.src: 可能就是因为这样，不止是武士，就连普通百姓也都在唾弃那些尸位素餐的卑劣武士。

en: It is said that last year Lord Okabayashi Mokunosuke was forced by his relatives to commit seppuku.
u.src: 据说去年冈林杢之助官老爷是被亲戚们逼迫才切腹自尽的。

ja: られなかったとしても、
わずにはいられなかっただろう。
en: But even if he had not been forced, with matters having come this far, he probably would have had to bear the disgrace.
u.src: 不过就是不遭遇被迫，事已至此，恐怕也不得不承担污名。

en: All the more so for the others.
u.src: 更遑论说其他人了。

en: Edo natives have always admired righteous courage, and now, following your example of avenging wrongs, the common people have long been indignant; at any moment they may kill those vile men.
u.src: 江户本地人原本就崇尚见义勇为，现如今效仿各位报仇雪恨，很久之前百姓们就为此感到愤慨，没准什么时候就把这些卑劣之人杀了呢。”

en: Den'emon declared this with surging passion, as if he were speaking about his own affair.
u.src: 传右卫门激情澎湃的断定说，就像在说自己的事情一样。

en: Judging from his posture, he seemed likely to be the first to take on the task of killing those men himself.
u.src: 看他那个姿态，他自己很可能第一个去承担杀掉那些人的任务呢。

en: Under his influence, Yoshida, Hara, Hayamizu, Horibe, and the others also grew fired up, and their denunciation of those traitorous rebels rose to a new pitch.
u.src: 在他的影响下，吉田、原、早水、堀部等人也都激昂起来，对那些乱臣贼子的痛骂又上升了一个新的层次。

en: But among them, only Oishi Kuranosuke sat with both hands on his knees, silently gazing at the brazier.
u.src: ——但是这其中只有石内藏助双手伏膝，一言不发的看着火盆。

en: He came to recognize a new fact: by shifting the subject and making an attack on his former friends who had defected its basis, their own acts of loyalty won even greater praise.
u.src: 他认清了一个新的事实：他把话题转移的后果，以抨击变节的故友为基础，他们的忠义行为受到了更多的赞扬。

en: Because of that, the spring breeze blowing through his heart once again carried away a little of its warmth.
u.src: 因此，吹拂在他心里的春风，再一次带走了几分温暖。

ja: えるためだけではない
en: To be sure, he did not grieve over those betrayers merely in order to change the subject,
u.src: 诚然，他不光是为了转移话题才痛惜那些背叛者、

en: In fact, he could not help feeling regret over their flight in the face of battle, and he felt deeply distressed by it as well.
u.src: 事实上，他对他们临阵脱逃的行为不禁觉得痛惜，也感到十分难过。

en: But although he felt pity for those disloyal warriors, he did not truly hate them.
u.src: 但是他虽然为那些不忠的务武士感到惋惜，但是却并不真的憎恨他们。

en: If the word frank can be used, then it was a very frank sort of pity.
u.src: 假如能够用率直这个词，那很是率直的可怜。

ja: そうであったからこそ
en: Precisely because he was always like this, he had in truth maintained a tolerant attitude toward them all along,
u.src: 就因为总这样，他其实一直对他们持有包容的态度，

en: and all the more so today, when his great vengeance had been fulfilled, he could only dismiss them with a pitying smile.
u.src: 更遑论在大仇得报的今天，对他们也只有可怜的一笑置之罢了。

en: The people of society seemed to think that even killing them would not be enough to dispel the hatred in their hearts.
u.src: 社会上的百姓好像都认为就算杀了他们也难消心头之恨。

en: Must praising us as loyal retainers necessarily mean lowering them into beasts dressed in human clothes?
u.src: 难道将我们捧作忠臣，就一定要贬低他们为衣冠禽兽呢？

en: There is no unbridgeable gulf between us and them.
u.src: 我们和他们之间并没有什么难以逾越的鸿沟。

en: Kuranosuke had long since come to feel disgust at the strange influence that had taken hold of the common people of Edo.
u.src: 内藏助对江户百姓受到的奇妙影响早就产生了厌恶心理。

en: Now, in the public opinion represented by Denemon, he again saw the influence that had affected those who had fled in this incident.
u.src: 如今他又在以传右卫门为代表的舆论中看到了这次临阵脱逃的人所受到的影响。

en: Although these two matters were essentially different, one could hardly blame him for feeling displeased.
u.src: 虽然说这两件事本质不同，但是也不能怪他感到不快了。

ja: まることになっていた
en: However, this was not the end of the matter; Kuranosuke's displeasure was destined to intensify once again.
u.src: 但是，这并不是事情的结束，藏助的不快注定要再次升级。

en: Seeing that he said nothing at all, Den'emon guessed that it might be because he was extremely modest in manner, and his admiration for him grew even stronger.
u.src: 传右卫门看到他一言不发，揣测他可能是因为态度十分谦虚，对他的钦佩之情更多了。

en: To express his admiration for Kuranosuke, the honest and dutiful Higo samurai forced the conversation in a new direction and immediately began praising loyal Kuranosuke:
u.src: 为了表达自己对内藏助的钦佩之心，老实本分的肥后武士硬把话题一转，马上开始了对忠义的内藏助的赞扬：

en: "I once heard a very learned man say,
u.src: “以前曾经听一位很有学问的人讲过，

en: In China there was a warrior who, in order to avenge his own lord, went so far as to swallow charcoal and become mute.
u.src: 中国有一位武士，为了给自己的主人复仇，不惜吞炭变成了哑巴。

en: But compared with Lord Kuranosuke's suffering, his pain was truly nothing beside it,
u.src: 但是他的痛苦跟内藏助大人的比起来，真是小巫见大巫，

ja: わねばならないからだ
en: because that great man must even go against his own wishes and pretend to be a dissolute wastrel."
u.src: 因为达人还要违背自己的意愿假装出放浪形骸的模样。”

en: Denemon first offered this preface, then began at great length to tell anecdotes of Kuranosuke's dissolute behavior a year earlier.
u.src: 传右卫门首先说了这样一段引子，接着开始长篇大论的讲起谈起内藏助一年前放浪形骸的逸事。

en: Even when he went to Takao and Atago to view the autumn leaves, he pretended to be mad; surely he must have been suffering terribly inside.
u.src: 去高尾和爱宕去赏红叶时他也装疯，心里肯定非常痛苦啊。

ja: しなければならなかったのだから、
en: Because he had to keep up that painful ruse, even attending cherry blossom banquets in Shimabara and Gion must surely have been terribly hard for him.
u.src: 因为一直要搞苦肉计，想必他在岛原和祇园参加赏樱花宴会也一定非常痛苦……

en: It is said that in Kyoto at the time, this comic verse was still being passed around:
“A paper-covered Oishi floats light as air; with nothing in his belly, he is only a straw sack.”
u.src: “‘纸糊大石轻飘飘，腹中无物是草包’，据说那时候京都还流传这首打油诗。

ja: くことなど、とうていできなかった。
en: Only by handling matters with such skill could he have deceived the people of the realm to this extent.
u.src: 如果不是巧妙做事，根本不可能欺骗天下百姓到这个程度。

en: When Lord Amano Yazaemon praised your courage and composure a little while ago, his judgment was entirely accurate.
u.src: 早些时候天野弥左卫门官人对您的勇敢沉着大加褒奖，是十分准确的。”

en: Oh no, not at all. I truly do not deserve such praise.
u.src: “哪里哪里，实在愧不敢当。”

en: Kuranosuke forced himself to say something in reply.
u.src: 内藏助勉为其难的搭话。

en: Den'emon saw that Kuranosuke was still modest and careful, worried that his own words had not been complete enough, and at the same time admired Kuranosuke's noble character all the more.
u.src: 传右卫门看内藏助还是一副谨慎小心的谦虚态度，生怕自己说的不够完整，与此同时更加敬佩他高尚的品行。

en: He had originally been addressing Kuranosuke, but now he turned again toward Onodera Junai, who was stationed in Kyoto, and showed his admiration even more eagerly than before.
u.src: 他原本是对着内藏助的，这个时候又开始向京都值勤的小野寺十内，比刚才更卖力气的展现自己的钦佩之心。

en: This childlike enthusiasm of his seemed both amusing and endearing to Junai, who was very learned,
u.src: 他这种稚童般的热情，让以学问很多的十内感到好笑又可爱，

en: So Junai kindly followed Den'emon's wishes and began to tell in detail how Kuranosuke had tried to deceive the spies sent by the enemy house,
u.src: 他厚道的顺着传右卫门的意思，详细的讲起了内藏助为了蒙骗仇人家派出的细作，

en: the story that he put on a Buddhist robe and spent his time in the room of Yugiri, the famous courtesan of Masuya.
u.src: 裹着法衣，流连于升屋的名妓夕雾屋里的逸事。

en: Even the solemn and earnest Kuranosuke wrote a song called Little Scenes of the Pleasure Quarter around that time.
u.src: “如此严肃认真的内藏助，那时候还写过《花街小景》这样一首歌。

en: The song became very popular in the pleasure quarters.
u.src: 这歌在花街柳巷十分流行。

en: And around then Kuranosuke, wrapped in a black Buddhist robe, would walk drunkenly through the falling cherry blossoms of Gion,
u.src: 而且那时候内藏助裹着黑色法衣，醉熏熏的行走在祇园零落的樱花中，

en: while the common people jeered and gave him the nickname of the frivolous young lord.
u.src: 百姓起哄的给他起了浮华公子的称号。

en: There was a reason why Little Scenes of the Pleasure Quarter was such a hit,
u.src: 《花街小景》这支歌之所以叫座儿，

en: and there was also a reason why Kuranosuke's dissolute behavior became so famous.
u.src: 内藏助的放浪行为之所以出名，都是有道理的。

en: Whether it was Yugiri, Ukihashi, or anyone else,
u.src: 不管是夕雾、浮桥也好，

en: or the famous tayu of Shimabara and Shumokumachi,
u.src: 还是岛原和撞木町的有名的太夫们，

en: as long as the guest was Kuranosuke, they all competed to receive him as an honored patron.
u.src: 只要是内藏助，就都争相奉其为座上宾。”

en: When Kuranosuke heard Junai speak of this, his feelings were tangled and bitter, as though he had been insulted.
u.src: 内藏助听十内说这件事，心里五味杂陈，像受到了侮辱一般。

en: Besides that, he could not help recalling his former dissipated behavior.
u.src: 此外，又情不自禁的回忆以前的放浪行为。

en: Those memories were vividly colored for him.
u.src: 那些对他来说色彩绚烂的回忆。

en: The light of long candles, the fragrance of aloeswood oil, and the sound of the shamisen playing Kaga ditties kept echoing in his mind.
u.src: 长蜡烛的光、沉香油的香气、三弦奏加贺小调的声音，始终回荡在他的脑海里。

en: Indeed, pearl-like tears fall pattering down, soaking the red sleeves; tears fall, a life of flesh, a bond as fleeting as dew,
u.src: “果然是，珠泪扑簌，把红袖湿遍，泪扑簌，皮肉生涯，露水缘”，

en: the scenes from the lyrics of Scenes of the Pleasure Quarter that Junai had mentioned,
u.src: 十内说起的《花街小景》的歌词中的场景，

en: and the bewitching Yugiri and Ukihashi, as alluring as if they had stepped out of the Eastern Palace, also drifted through his mind.
u.src: 和魅力妖娆的如同出自东宫的夕雾和浮桥，也飘荡在他脑海里。

en: He had once enjoyed a life of reckless pleasure so completely.
u.src: 他曾经如此尽情的享受过放浪形骸的生活啊。

en: In that unrestrained life, he had many times felt as happy as an immortal and had put revenge out of his mind.
u.src: 在那段不羁的生活里，很多次他感到快乐似神仙，将复仇抛之脑后。

en: He was an honest and rational man, and he did not want to deny those facts by deceiving himself.
u.src: 他是个正直而理智的人，不想自欺欺人的否定那些事实。

en: Of course, being deeply versed in human nature, he never dreamed that this was immoral.
u.src: 当然，深谙人性的他，做梦也不认为这件事是违背道德的。

en: Precisely for that reason, having his dissipation treated as a means of loyal service both displeased him and made him feel guilty.
u.src: 就因为这样，对他的放浪形骸都看做尽忠的一种手段，既让他感到不快又让他觉得愧疚。

en: This was what Kuranosuke thought in his heart,
u.src: 内藏助心里如是想，

en: so it was only natural that he felt displeased when others praised his act of pretending to be mad,
u.src: 他对别人称赞自己装疯卖傻的行为感到不快，
也就顺理成章了。
他觉得，

en: the last faint spring breeze that had been blowing through his heart
u.src: 吹拂在心里的最后一点春风，

en: had lost every trace of warmth after this blow.
u.src: 经此打击一点温暖都没有了。

en: Now only a cold shadow remained in his heart.
u.src: 如今他心里只剩下冰冷的阴影了。

en: He did not like being misunderstood,
u.src: 他不喜欢被误解，

en: and at the same time, because this misunderstanding had been beyond anything he expected,
u.src: 同时又因为这种误解在自己意料之外，

en: he also felt dejected by his own incompetence and foolishness.
u.src: 而对自己的无能和愚蠢也感觉沮丧。
他的复仇壮举，

en: his comrades, and even he himself
u.src: 他的同伴，还有他本人，

en: might perhaps be remembered for generations because of this careless praise.
u.src: 可能会因着这种随意的赞扬而流芳百世吧。
——想到这令人不快的事情，

en: he held his hands over the charcoal fire that was about to go out, warming them,
u.src: 他把手放在就要熄灭的炭火上烘着，

en: no longer looking at Denemon's eyes,
u.src: 没再看传右卫门的眼神，
凄凉的叹了一口气。

en: After a few minutes had passed, Oishi Kuranosuke falsely said he was going to the privy and left his seat; alone, he leaned against a veranda pillar and quietly looked at the vivid plum blossoms blooming among the moss and stones in the old garden.
u.src: 过了约莫几分钟，大石内藏助谎称去如厕离席，他一个人靠着檐廊的柱子，静静看着古老庭院里青苔和石头中间开放的鲜艳梅花。

en: The evening sun was fading, and dusk had begun to stain the bamboo grove in the garden.
u.src: 夕阳日薄，暮色侵染了院中竹林。

en: Yet inside the paper sliding doors, the lively, spirited discussion was still going on.
u.src: 可是，纸拉门内还在兴致勃勃的高谈阔论。

en: As he listened to their cheerful conversation, he felt sorrow closing around him, and with the fragrance of the plum blossoms it chilled him all the way to the depths of his heart.
u.src: 听着他们谈笑风生，他觉得悲哀包围了自己，伴随着梅花的香气，一直凉到自己的内心深处。

en: Where, after all, had this loneliness, this indescribable loneliness, come from?
u.src: 这种寂寞，这种难以名状的寂寞，究竟是从何而来的呢——

en: Kuranosuke raised his head and gazed at the cold white blossoms that seemed to be set into the sky, standing there for a long time.
u.src: 内藏助抬头望着好像镶嵌在天空中冰冷洁白的花朵，久久的站在那里。
